spot: Ben Shelton ended Carlos Alcaraz’s U.S. Open title reign in a historic late-night marathon match, securing a 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 victory that concluded at 3:33 a.m. This monumental win also snapped Alcaraz's impressive 18-match Grand Slam winning streak.
content_html:
Key Developments

In a dramatic turn at the U.S. Open, American tennis player Ben Shelton delivered a stunning upset, defeating defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a grueling five-set battle. The match, which stretched into the early hours of the morning, concluded at an unprecedented 3:33 a.m., marking it as the latest-finishing match in the tournament's storied history.

Shelton emerged victorious with a final score of 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6, showcasing remarkable resilience and skill against the world-renowned Spaniard. The intense contest saw both players push their limits, with momentum swinging back and forth across the sets.

For Carlos Alcaraz, the defeat signifies the end of his dominant run at Grand Slam tournaments, as his impressive 18-match winning streak was brought to a halt. Alcaraz, who was aiming to defend his U.S. Open title, faced a formidable challenge from Shelton, who demonstrated his potential on the grand stage.

Following this monumental victory, Ben Shelton is set to advance further in the U.S. Open, where he will face fellow American Frances Tiafoe in what promises to be another highly anticipated match.

Key Takeaways

  • Ben Shelton defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set thriller at the U.S. Open.
  • The match made history by concluding at 3:33 a.m., becoming the latest finish ever at the tournament.
  • Shelton's victory ended Alcaraz's 18-match Grand Slam winning streak and his U.S. Open title reign.

Why It Matters

This match is significant for several reasons. It not only sets a new record for the latest finish in U.S. Open history but also represents a major upset in the tournament. Ben Shelton's triumph over a top-ranked player like Carlos Alcaraz highlights the emergence of new talent in men's tennis and signals a potential shift in the competitive landscape. For Alcaraz, the loss is a rare setback, ending a remarkable streak and opening the door for other contenders. The late-night drama captivated audiences and underscored the physical and mental demands of Grand Slam tennis, adding another memorable chapter to the U.S. Open's legacy.
